static_traits.name: Chen Ran
static_traits.social_status: Has several close friends, but usually does not discuss feelings of giving up easily with them; tends to avoid competitive situations with friends
static_traits.medical_history: No psychotherapy history; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Positive attitude, willing to change; using absolutist expressions when talking about failure (such as 'I never will...'); tending to focus on the negative and using avoidance as the main coping

basic_info.main_problem: I tend to give up easily after failure; recently after losing a video game ranked match felt I would never play again; this pattern has worsened recently, leading me to avoid games and other competitive situations.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize that this pattern of readily giving up after failure is negatively affecting my enjoyment of video games and the guitar, so I am seeking counseling.
growth_experiences: For a long time, in competitive situations such as academics and games, often used complete avoidance as the main coping after failure (stopping participation in activities); never received psychotherapy; always held high expectations for oneself, initially moderate pressure, gradually worsening recently and extending to Work and daily interests (such as cooking, playing guitar).

Although overall performance at Work is Good, tending to avoid challenging projects due to fear of failure; this tendency has repeatedly occurred in the past, and affects competitive interactions with friends.

special_situations.event: The most recent ranked match loss in a video game
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I fail, it shows I am not good enough, continuing to play is meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately stops the game and avoids participating in ranked matches again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never play this game again/I will not succeed

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If success cannot be ensured, one should not try; failure will prove I am incapable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding participation or pushing away challenging projects
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will probably fail, better not to do it

special_situations.event: Being in competitive activities or settings with friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I perform worse than others, it equals failure, embarrassing me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to avoid competitive activities with friends
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am inferior to them, participating will only make things worse

special_situations.event: Encountering setbacks when trying to cook new dishes or practice guitar
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Doing poorly once shows I am incapable in this area
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Stops trying new dishes or reduces practice
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Not doing well this time proves I am not skilled, better not to continue

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized in competition and challenges and to prove own worth
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure leading to self-worth being negated, triggering strong frustration and pressure
defense_goal: Maintains the stability of self-esteem and emotions by avoiding competition and challenges

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough failure (once failing, negating oneself completely)
object_relations.object_representation: Picky and judgmental others or competitors (who might embarrass me)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked to review failures or invited to try challenging tasks (for example discussing 'recent failures' or 'doing small experiments' in counseling)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Viewing one failure as evidence of permanent failure, believing continued attempts will only prove oneself 'incapable' (transference: experiencing others' expectations as judgment)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a gentle, non-judgmental tone, acknowledging their feelings, hinting at gray areas and continuums; Guiding them to discover partial successes and Learning points through open-ended Questioning, avoiding absolutist words.

manifestations: In interests such as video games, guitar, and cooking, easily gives up due to failure, subjective enjoyment significantly declines
Avoiding competition narrows life experiences, making it hard to gain satisfaction from activities
Reducing choice and action Freedom due to fear of failure, tending to only do things that ensure success
Interprets one failure as a permanent limitation, losing the sense of self-direction

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequently evaluating oneself in absolutist language (such as 'I am not good enough' 'I will never succeed')
Finds it hard to recall successful experiences; mainly focuses on failures
Before competitive situations, excessive self-scrutiny leads to choosing avoidance

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves.
manifestations: Choosing to turn energy into self-Withdrawal and stopping action when facing the urge of challenges or competition (such as stopping games, avoiding projects)
Tending not to express to or seek support from friends, instead digesting alone and retreating

positive_force: Overall Good Work performance, with stable occupational functioning
Has a few friends to talk with (potential support resources)
Willing to change, Positive attitude, willing to try identifying and restructuring automatic thoughts
Able to identify one's own problem patterns (noticing 'giving up easily after failure')
negative_force: High Fear of failure and all-or-nothing thinking
Mental filtering, pays more attention to negative experiences, difficult to recall successes
Avoidance as the main coping strategy limits attempts and growth

target_behavior.behavior: Immediately giving up and avoiding competitive/challenging activities after experiencing or Anticipating failure
antecedent: Losing in a ranked video game match
Being in a competitive scenario with friends
Encounters setbacks when trying new dishes or practicing guitar
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing and all-or-nothing cognition about failure (one failure equals permanent failure/not good enough), plus long-term high expectations and over-binding self-worth to success and failure
target_behavior.function: Escaping the Anxiety and Self-denial brought by failure, to relieve pressure in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Declining interest and fun, skill Learning and development hindered, Career development limited, Reduced social interaction and avoidance
